summary:
ANTRIKSH is a planetary analog intelligence system that helps identify and evaluate Earth locations with environmental and terrain characteristics comparable to selected regions on the Moon and Mars.

Finding suitable terrestrial analogs is important for preparing exploration missions, testing rover mobility, studying extreme environments, and understanding the challenges posed by extraterrestrial terrain. ANTARIKSH addresses this by combining planetary reference profiles with Earth observation datasets to systematically screen and rank potential analog locations.

The platform evaluates 78,247 land cells across six environmental and terrain criteria, including precipitation, vegetation, temperature variation, land surface temperature, slope, and terrain roughness. An explainable weighted scoring model ranks candidate locations, while interactive 3D visualizations allow users to inspect terrain characteristics in detail.

By connecting planetary science with Earth observation, ANTARIKSH transforms global environmental data into an interactive tool for discovering and investigating potential planetary analog sites.
details:
What ANTRIKSH Does

ANTRIKSH is an interactive planetary analog discovery platform designed to help researchers, mission planners, and exploration teams identify locations on Earth that resemble selected regions of the Moon and Mars.

The system begins with a planetary target profile. It compares the environmental characteristics of that target against a global collection of Earth land cells and identifies locations with similar conditions.

How It Works

1. Planetary Reference Profiles

Users select from five built-in lunar and Martian target profiles. Each profile provides the reference environmental characteristics against which terrestrial locations are evaluated.

2. Global Earth Screening

ANTRIKSH screens 78,247 land cells using six criteria:

  • Precipitation
  • Vegetation index (NDVI)
  • Annual temperature range
  • Day–night land surface temperature variation
  • Terrain slope
  • Terrain roughness

3. Explainable Similarity Scoring

A weighted geometric mean model combines the six criteria into an overall similarity score. The platform ranks potential analog locations and provides criterion-wise breakdowns to explain how each candidate compares with the selected planetary target.

4. Interactive Discovery

A 3D Earth globe and suitability heatmap enable users to explore the geographic distribution of potential analogs. Users can inspect ranked candidates and navigate from global discovery to individual locations.

5. Detailed Terrain Intelligence

The God's Eye interface provides an immersive 3D view of selected terrain, supported by elevation profiles and terrain measurements. This helps users investigate elevation variation, slope characteristics, relief, and other factors relevant to analog-site evaluation.

Why It Matters

Planetary analog environments on Earth provide valuable opportunities to study geological conditions, evaluate exploration technologies, and prepare for the challenges of operating in extraterrestrial environments.

ANTRIKSH makes the initial discovery and comparison process more systematic, transparent, and accessible. Instead of relying solely on isolated locations or manual comparisons, users can screen a large geographic area, understand why a location ranks highly, and investigate its terrain through interactive visualizations.

Technology and Tools

The platform uses a web-based interactive architecture combining geospatial data processing, environmental similarity analysis, interactive mapping, and 3D terrain visualization. Its implementation includes React-based web technologies, geospatial visualization, 3D rendering, and a deterministic, explainable scoring model.

Creativity and Innovation

ANTRIKSH brings planetary reference environments and global Earth observation into one discovery workflow. Its combination of large-scale screening, explainable ranking, interactive geographic exploration, and detailed 3D terrain inspection creates a bridge between planetary science and practical terrestrial field research.
